name: Majestic Million (top 1M domains by referring subnets)
what_it_holds: Freely downloadable CSV (~80MB, CC BY 3.0 licensed) of the top 1 million root domains ranked by referring subnets/IPs, regenerated daily from Majestic's own crawl/link index; columns include GlobalRank, TLD, RefSubNets, RefIPs, rank deltas. Hosted at majestic.com/reports/majestic-million, not on GitHub itself, though community GitHub mirrors of historical snapshots exist sporadically (not verified this pass).
why_useful: A free, dated, backlink-based domain-authority ranking that could track airbnb.com vs vrbo.com/booking.com/expedia.com over time if snapshots are saved daily going forward (gap 19 adjacent: backlink/authority as an engagement proxy). No historical archive by default — would need our own daily pull starting now.
time_coverage: daily snapshot only (no historical archive without self-collection)
themes: Search/SEO and referral data: Bing/Google keyword volume tools, SERP scrapers, Common Crawl web graph, backlink datasets, AI-bot crawler traffic stats (Cloudflare, Vercel)
why_all: A free, dated, backlink-based domain-authority ranking that could track airbnb.com vs vrbo.com/booking.com/expedia.com over time if snapshots are saved daily going forward (gap 19 adjacent: backlink/authority as an engagement proxy). name: google-covid-19-community-mobility-reports

why_useful: Confirms an auto-refreshing distribution channel existed (daily cadence claimed) but the actual bytes live on AWS Data Exchange, not GitHub, and the source report itself is discontinued — lower value than ActiveConclusion's committed CSVs.

name: QuantConnect/Lean.DataSource.QuiverQuant
what_it_holds: QuantConnect's official LEAN integration/connector for Quiver Quantitative's alternative-data feed (congressional trading, WSB sentiment, Wikipedia pageview trends, Twitter followers, insider/lobbying data). Code defines the data schema and pulls live from Quiver's (paid) API into LEAN backtests; no historical data committed. Sibling repos: Lean.DataSource.QuiverQuantCongressTrading, ...WallStreetBets, ...Wikipedia, ...TwitterFollowers (all last pushed 2023-2026, low stars 0-7).
why_useful: Quiver's actual datasets (Congress trading, WSB sentiment, Wikipedia pageviews) are not travel-demand series and don't map to a numbered gap directly, though the Wikipedia-pageviews sibling repo (Lean.DataSource.QuiverQuantWikipedia) is a possible ABNB-pageviews engagement proxy (gap 5) if the API were free, which it is not for bulk history.
themes: Alternative-data vendor sample repos: vendors publishing free samples on GitHub (Advan, Similarweb, Apptopia, Yipit-like, Consumer Edge, Earnest, M Science, Quiver Quant, Thinknum)
why_all: Quiver's actual datasets (Congress trading, WSB sentiment, Wikipedia pageviews) are not travel-demand series and don't map to a numbered gap directly, though the Wikipedia-pageviews sibling repo (Lean.DataSource.QuiverQuantWikipedia) is a possible ABNB-pageviews engagement proxy (gap 5) if the API were free, which it is not for bulk history.

Quiver's Wikipedia-pageview and social-sentiment feeds could proxy engagement/brand-interest trends for ABNB or peers (gap #5) if paired with a Quiver API key; the connector code documents exact field schemas even without data access.

name: QuantConnect/Lean.DataSource.QuiverQuantWikipedia
what_it_holds: Example implementation pulling QuiverQuant's Wikipedia pageview dataset (per-ticker Wikipedia page pageviews) via QuantConnect's paid data marketplace. No historical CSV committed.
why_useful: Wikipedia pageviews for the ABNB article could be an engagement/awareness proxy (gap 5); however this repo is only a connector to a paid feed, not a free source — Wikipedia's own pageviews API (wikimedia REST API) is free and better suited, and this repo is not that.
